page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It is configured with 1 physical core and 1 vCPU, providing a dedicated CPU allocation with 1 thread per core. The hardware profile includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities due to the single-vCPU configuration. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, and achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, fall into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block and large block bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10%. Similarly, database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations perform in the bottom 10% of tested systems.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-1 offers a low-entry hardware profile with dedicated CPU resources, avoiding the performance unpredictability of shared-core burstable instances. However, the resource density is low, and the single-vCPU limit restricts its utility for parallel processing or memory-intensive tasks. It is suitable for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, simple utility scripting, or small-scale development and testing environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or multi-core execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance equipped with a single dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 vCPU and 4.0 GB of RAM. It features a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng single-core tests, alongside average single-threaded compression and text processing speeds. However, its single-vCPU design results in poor multi-core performance, low memory bandwidth, and weak database and web-serving throughput, all placing in the bottom 10% to 25%. This instance provides a cost-effective entry point with dedicated CPU resources, making it suitable for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic utility scripts, and small-scale development environments rather than parallel processing or data-intensive workloads.
